question: Why does the golfer leading a tournament after the first round so often fade by the last day?
answer: Because a first-round lead takes skill plus an unusually lucky day, and the luck does not carry over. Connolly and Rendleman modelled thousands of PGA Tour rounds: the top finishers in an event had typically enjoyed well above average luck. Among 150 players someone always has a hot round; next day the dice roll again.
move: The top of any list holds the luckiest as well as the best.
ask: When I compare myself with the very top, how much of their position is luck I cannot copy?
source: Connolly & Rendleman, J Am Stat Assoc, 2008
reference: Robert A. Connolly & Richard J. Rendleman, Skill, Luck, and Streaky Play on the PGA Tour, Journal of the American Statistical Association, 2008
